label: early-position gate: o/a/u/r/q/d/c at step 0 or 3, and <DEL> in short (L<=4) sequences
explanation: Active only at steps 0-4 and never in the copy phase after the delimiter. It has three parts: (1) step 0 when the first token is one of o,a,u,r,q,d,c (precision 1.0, and this covers every step-0 activation; o is the strongest); (2) the <DEL> step, only when L<=4, and these are the largest activations (top examples are <DEL> with L=3, about 0.12, especially after s/t inputs); (3) original-phase step 3, mostly on the same seven letters. Step 3 is the noisy part: about 40% of step-3 activations are on other tokens, depending on history. There are small leftovers at steps 2 and 4 (about 4% of mass). It never fires at step 1, at step >= 5, or on repeated tokens (in_first=0 carries 2% of mass). Dev F1 0.79, mass recall 0.86.
